25de0d48:
hydra: a Houdini ramp finally fills the table Cycles expects

Color Ramp, RGB Curves, Vector Curves and Float Curve computed nothing at all.
Their socket is an array, and compile() gives up on the first line when that
array is empty: the node's output is not even a default color, it is whatever
was lying on the compiler's stack.

Houdini does write the ramp, but in its own encoding: an integer `<name>`
holding the number of keys, a `<name>_keys` of positions, a `<name>_values` of
values and a `<name>_basis` of interpolation. Cycles wants a flat table with a
constant step.

So we gather the four and resample to RAMP_TABLE_SIZE, honoring the basis --
constant, linear, Catmull-Rom. The alpha channel, which Houdini's ramp does not
carry, is filled with opaque: without it the two arrays do not have the same
size and Cycles gives up again.

These parameters are removed from the ordinary loop, otherwise the key count,
an integer, would land on the array socket itself.

a3d07f40:
hydra: deformation blur for animated points

Motion blur only covered what moves as a whole. Geometry whose points are
animated -- a simulation, a deformer, particles, hair -- rendered sharp even
though the rest of the scene blurred correctly: the more visible of the two
defects, since nothing signals that the blur is missing.

The positions are sampled along the shutter, at the same evenly spaced times as
the transforms, because Cycles spreads its motion steps linearly -- uneven
sampling would blur along a distorted trajectory. Cycles stores these steps in
the position attribute itself, with the center step at index 0.

All three geometries benefit, the mesh, the curves and the point cloud, through
shared sampling. The shutter is kept on the geometry because Populate() does
not see the render param.

One case is deliberately set aside: a point count that changes from one instant
to the next. Geometry created or destroyed mid-shot has no correspondence to
interpolate, so we stick to the center instant rather than mix unrelated
points.

5207cd12:
hydra: velocity blur, for geometry whose point count varies

Position sampling does not cover everything. As soon as the point count changes
from one frame to the next, there is no correspondence left to interpolate --
and that is exactly what a simulation produces. Houdini then writes a single
point sample and a `velocities` field. Without reading that field, such
geometry cannot be rendered with blur.

Verified before writing anything: neither USD nor Hydra synthesizes the
positions for us. A mesh with `velocities` rendered sharp, at its rest
position.

Velocities now take precedence over interpolation between samples, as USD
prescribes. Two points of caution:

* USD velocities are in units per second and the shutter is in frames:
  without timeCodesPerSecond, read from the scene globals, neither tells how
  long the other lasts;
* `accelerations`, if written, bend the trajectory to second order -- a
  projectile blurs along its arc and not along its chord.

At equal amplitude, the velocity cube and the sampled-points cube blur by the
same length.

0d51aeeb:
hydra: per-corner normals, instead of faceting what is not faceted

The previous fix read the mesh normals rather than the display index, but
honored only three interpolations -- vertex, varying, constant -- and took
`faceVarying` as the mark of a hard edge. Yet that is precisely what Houdini
writes as soon as the normal lives on the vertices, its common case: a mesh
with smooth normals rendered faceted.

The code carried the reason, which has become false: "Cycles has no per-corner
normals", with the real handling behind an #if 0. ATTR_STD_CORNER_NORMAL now
exists, kernel support included.

Per-corner normals are therefore written as they are, triangulated like the
topology. Cycles then stops consulting the smooth/flat flag -- the hardness of
an edge is already inscribed in the gap between the normals of its corners. The
mesh decides, edge by edge, instead of suffering a choice imposed on the whole
piece.

Verified: the same normals, stored per corner or per point, render the exact
same image bit for bit; and a mesh without normals stays faceted, which is the
right answer since there is nothing to interpolate.

The flag keeps a fallback role. Cycles discards per-corner normals when the
geometry blurs without the normals moving along with it; it is better to smooth
approximately than to facet outright what the mesh never asked for.

1ba447fd:
scene: displacement was added to itself on every material edit

Changing a displacement value in the viewport stacked the displacements: each
edit added its own to the relief already computed, and a Restart Render was
needed to get the right shape back.

`read_shader_output` writes `verts[v] = verts[v] + off`. Cycles therefore
relies on the host to restore the original positions before each new
computation - Blender does it by re-exporting the mesh - whereas modifying the
displacement triggers this computation by itself: `GeometryManager::device_update`
marks the mesh position as modified as soon as `shader->need_update_displacement`
(geometry.cpp). A host that only touches the shader has no reason to send points
again, and ends up displacing an already displaced mesh.

A subdivided mesh escaped this: the same function also marks the dicing as
modified, so the tessellation redoes the vertices. A polygonal mesh did not.

The ATTR_STD_POSITION_UNDISPLACED attribute already existed, but only when a
shader requested the undisplaced position. It is now taken as soon as a mesh
carries a real displacement, and `read_shader_output` starts from it: the
computation becomes idempotent. On the delegate side, setting new points
discards this backup, otherwise animated geometry would start again from the
previous pose.

Measured, 40x40 non-subdivided grid, scale 0.4 on frame 1 then 0.8 on frame 2,
husk rendering both in the same session; difference of frame 2 from the same
frame rendered alone:

    sphere      no/yes      1.014
    rectangle   no/yes      1.014

e5371777:
hydra: transmission and subsurface colors, finally translated

Two standard_surface inputs went nowhere, and the audit said why: Cycles tints
transmission and subsurface with the same `base_color`, so multiplying them
into it also stained the diffuse. The objection holds for a plain
multiplication; it falls with the right setup.

**transmission_color** goes through a `mix_color` driven by
`light_path.is_transmission_ray`: the ray passing through sees the transmission
color, all the others the base color. Measured control: an opaque material
given a green transmission_color renders the same image to the pixel (difference
0.00000), whereas a glass goes from 0.516 neutral to (0.519 / 0.265 / 0.265)
with a red transmission_color.

**subsurface_color** tints the base color **in proportion to the subsurface
weight**: none at 0, full at 1. This is exact at both ends, the principled
mixing diffuse and subsurface by that same weight and coloring both with
base_color. Measured: neutral reference (2.01) -> (2.01 / 0.74 / 0.44) with a
red subsurface_color.

The other route, the one that multiplies the *radius* by the color, was tried
and **inverts the tint** - a red subsurface_color gives a cyan object, red
diffusing further instead of coming back out: (2.01 / 3.01 / 3.17) measured. It
is discarded for that reason.

In passing, the MaterialX default of the scattering radius, (1, 1, 1), is set
explicitly: Cycles' is (1, 0.2, 0.1) - a skin - and since Hydra only passes the

1cff67de:
hydra: a texture that changes, and a camera one leaves

Two irritants reported, both solved until now by a Restart Render done by hand.

**A texture did not reload.** `ImageTextureNode::update_images` only asks the
manager for its image if the node's `handle` is empty: once the image is loaded,
writing another file name on the socket does not replace it. A rebuilt graph - a
Restart Render, or any edit that dirties the resource - started again from new
nodes and masked the defect; an edit that only touched parameters kept the old
image. The handle is now emptied as soon as one of the sockets that describe the
image has changed, and Cycles asks for it again. Its manager recognizes the same
image, so nothing is reloaded for nothing.

**Leaving a camera, or entering one**, changes the source of the view without
necessarily changing a value of the Cycles camera node: the framing could stay
that of the previous one, the view no longer respond, until a Restart Render.
The switch is now detected and counts as a reset of the session, which is what
that Restart Render did.

⚠️ The trap, found by living it: a render pass can be built anew on every pass -
this is the case in batch - so the first observation must **not** count as a
switch. Without this guard, the session restarted from zero on every pass and
the render no longer accumulated anything: a scene that takes 4.5 s was still
running after ten minutes, repeating "Rendered 1 samples" endlessly.

Tried and discarded, the way that consists in applying the matrices of the pass
state on top of the camera prim: the values reconstructed from a projection
differ from those of the prim, the camera node ends up modified on every frame,
and the session restarts from zero indefinitely - same symptom.

`UsdPreviewSurface`. A Cycles material being neither, it came out gray - no
color, no texture, no roughness, no normal.

Solaris does provide the bridge, though: next to the engine's own shader, it
writes a `UsdPreviewSurface` built by a "preview shader translator". The
original one reads `ogl_*` tags set on the VOP's parameters; our nodes are

`cycles_image_texture`, we also know which file to read. This is the method of

not on the surface shader.

67770647:
hydra: stop flipping COP images, both ends already store them alike

The previous fix added a flip at read time. It was one too many, and it is what
put the texture upside down. Two measurements say so.

On the Houdini side: a `uvmap` COP read through `allBufferElements` gives V =
-0.999 on the **first** row of the buffer and +0.999 on the last. The first row
is therefore the bottom of the image.

On the Cycles side: its file reader calls OIIO with `flip_y = true` by default
(`ImageMetaData::oiio_load_pixels`) - a negative row stride starting from the
last row, so the top row of the file lands at the end of the buffer. The first
row of a Cycles image is also the bottom.

The two conventions were already identical; making them disagree flipped the
image. The read becomes a `memcpy` again.

Calibrated on the file path, which does not go through us: a PNG red at the top
and blue at the bottom, placed on a plane whose v is 1 at the top, comes out red
at the top - red measured at y=20, blue at y=44 on a 64-pixel render.

The lesson, for the third time on this subject: a storage convention is read in
the code of whoever sets it, not in an image you look at.

0d6ecd81:
hydra: MaterialX hair, and the surface node that cut everything

Reported: impossible to shade hair in MaterialX with Cycles. Five nodes were
missing, and the dumbest of them cut everything: `surface`, which turns a bare
BSDF into a surface shader. Without it, the terminal received nothing.

chiang_hair_bsdf becomes Cycles' principled hair, Chiang's model, parameterized
by absorption. MaterialX and Cycles implement the same paper with the same
polynomials; only the step where each converts the roughness changes. MaterialX
converts it in chiang_hair_roughness and gives the BSDF a variance, whereas
Cycles expects the "artist" roughness and converts itself. So
chiang_hair_roughness passes it through as is, and a roughness written as a
value on the BSDF is brought back to beta by inverting the polynomials. TT and
TRT have no roughness of their own in Cycles, which derives them as v/4 and 4v -
MaterialX's default scales.

Absorption from a color and from melanin are redone node by node: MaterialX's
melanin does not have the constants of Cycles', relying on it would have changed
the hue.

Verified against known results: the MaterialX BSDF renders identical bit for bit
to Cycles' native principled hair; melanin, color and roughness as values agree
to within 2e-4; the material built with Houdini's mtlx nodes renders identical
to the test scene.

azimuthal roughness plugged in must reach the five terms of the absorption
polynomial, not just the first.

widths and the primvars; `varying` values are interpolated between the two
nearest. The common case - open non-indexed polylines - still copies the arrays
as they are.

camera. By default a linear curve is now an exact thick polyline, a cubic a round
tube; the cycles:curve_shape setting (auto, thick, ribbon) changes without
recompiling and redoes the curves already synchronized. Points (pointcloud) read

a0aab6bd:
hydra: the pass no longer blocks the UI, and the COP cache empties

The render pass took the scene lock by waiting: while the render thread updated
the device after an edit - a BVH can take seconds - Houdini's interface stayed
frozen. It now tries the lock; if the scene is busy, it marks its buffers as
non-converged, which makes the pass re-execute on the next refresh, where
everything is recomputed from the pass state: nothing is lost, unlike the old
try_lock. After ten consecutive postponements it waits, so that an edit is never
pushed back for good.

half floats weighs 256 MB, a few edits of a COP network filled the memory. An
entry that no material uses anymore leaves the cache when its last user is
forgotten, and when the cache exceeds its budget (HDCYCLES_COP_CACHE_MB, 4096 by
default). Cycles' image nodes keep their own reference: evicting never removes
an image from a render in progress.
